title: Gap 2: Coefficient bound $\mu_j\le 1/(2\sqrt2)$ — the crux constant

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (vertex coefficient bound).** After summing the four per-face inequalities of Gap 1, each vertex distance $\operatorname{dist}(p,V_j)$ appears with total coefficient $\mu_j=\sum_{i:\,V_j\in F_i}\lambda_{ij}$ (sum over the three faces incident to $V_j$). Prove
$$\mu_j\ \le\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\qquad\text{for every vertex }j\text{ and every tetrahedron},$$
so that $D_2(p)\le\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\sum_j\operatorname{dist}(p,V_j)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}D_0(p)$, i.e. $D_0\ge 2\sqrt2\,D_2$.

**This is where the constant $2\sqrt2$ is produced and is the hardest step.** The optimization is over the trihedral solid angle at $V_j$. NOTE (numerically certified in workspace): the regular tetrahedron with $p$ at the centroid gives ratio **exactly $3$**, NOT the extremum — so the worst case is asymmetric/degenerate and standard symmetry or SOS reductions can miss it. Expect the supremum of $\mu_j$ to sit on the boundary of the angle-parameter space (two coincident vertices, volume $\to 0$). A careful KKT/boundary analysis is required, and equality $\mu_j=1/(2\sqrt2)$ should hold only in that degenerate limit.
